name: New York
nameStory: It was New Amsterdam, run by the Dutch, until an English fleet sailed into the harbor in 1664 and demanded surrender. Governor Peter Stuyvesant wanted to fight; the townspeople refused, and the colony changed hands without a shot. The English renamed it for the king's brother, the Duke of York.
capitalStory: Albany is named for the same man - 'Duke of Albany' was his Scottish title. It became and stayed the capital because of where it sits: at the head of navigation on the Hudson, exactly where the Erie Canal later met the river, making it the hinge between the ocean and the entire interior.

majorFeatures.name: Hudson River
majorFeatures.note: A tidal estuary navigable 150 miles inland

funFacts: The Erie Canal, finished in 1825, linked the Great Lakes to the Atlantic and turned New York City into the dominant port in America almost overnight.
Adirondack Park is larger than Yellowstone, Yosemite, Grand Canyon, Glacier, and Olympic combined.
Niagara Falls erodes upstream about a foot a year; it has moved seven miles since the last ice age.
Manhattan's skyscrapers cluster downtown and midtown because that is where the hard bedrock is close enough to the surface to build on.
whyItMatters: About 12 million immigrants entered the United States through Ellis Island between 1892 and 1954. Something like 40% of Americans alive today have an ancestor who came through that one building in New York Harbor.
